transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As we all know, our cross-functional retrospective currently meets for 60 minutes every Thursday afternoon, and several of you have raised that interruptions and improvised exercises are making it harder to discuss problems candidly. On top of that, our current facilitator is leaving at the end of the month. So we've got both a pain point to address and a transition to manage. I'd love to hear your thoughts on what's been getting in the way and what we might want to change about the format going forward.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. I think the interruptions and improvised exercises are a real issue, and I'm glad we're talking about it before the facilitator transition. For me personally, I've found it hard to engage fully when exercises or prompts come together informally on the day of the meeting — I need time to prepare properly. I'd really like to propose that, going forward, any discussion questions or exercise prompts be circulated in writing at least 48 hours in advance. I think that would make the retrospective more productive for everyone, not just me.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thanks, Renee — that's a really concrete and actionable proposal. Circulating prompts 48 hours in advance directly addresses the candidness concern, since people can come prepared rather than feeling put on the spot. I'd want to make sure we capture that as a specific recommendation. Before we settle on anything, though, I'd like to hear from others — does the 48-hour advance notice resonate, or are there other format changes you'd want to see alongside it? And does anyone have thoughts on how we should handle the facilitator transition itself?

On the facilitator transition, I'd like to put something on the table: I've previously agreed to serve as the neutral timekeeper for the first six revised sessions. That could help address the interruption issue directly — having someone dedicated to keeping time and managing speaking order — while we settle into whatever new format we decide on. I don't think that solves the facilitator gap entirely, but it could be one piece of the bridge. I'd also note that I've been tracking interruptions informally this quarter, and I've seen it happen on a few occasions, so the concern people are raising is grounded in real patterns, not just perception. I haven't put those observations into the process notes yet, but I can do that if it would be helpful for the group to have a record.

commitments.detail: Full agenda including discussion questions, prompts, and any interactive exercises will be circulated in writing at least 48 hours in advance of each retrospective session.
Jon will serve as neutral timekeeper for the first six revised retrospective sessions, managing speaking order and keeping time to reduce interruptions.
Jon will add his informal interruption observations to the process notes to establish a baseline for tracking whether format changes are working.
No unmoderated role-play or unmoderated live exercises will be included in the retrospective format. Any interactive elements must be disclosed in the advance agenda.
The broader facilitator role to replace the departing facilitator remains an open item to be resolved before the end of the month transition.
